title: Micro-reservoir phase decoupling with attention-cost guided kernel selection
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Design and implement a micro-reservoir phase decoupler for prefill/decode flows that separates short-latency critical microphases from throughput-oriented longer phases. Integrate an attention-cost estimator to drive dynamic kernel selection (high-precision vs quantized fast kernels) per micro-reservoir, and add a fairness-smoothing layer that amortizes token credits across tenants to reduce starvation and latency spikes. This ticket covers design, simulator, small-scale perf experiments, and a gated rollout path for dedicated & hosted clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc published with API for micro-reservoir hints and kernel budget annotations (owner: runtime team)
Simulator shows >=15% tail-latency reduction (p99) for small prompt workloads with <=5% throughput loss on mixed traffic
Kernel probe mechanism implemented: online estimator picks kernel variant per micro-reservoir and records chosen kernel metrics
Fairness-smoothing reduces observed tenant starvation incidents in benchmark harness by >=40%
End-to-end integration tests and e2e perf job added to CI; can toggle feature flag at runtime
notes: Micro-reservoir = logical grouping of requests/windows smaller than existing phase windows; intended to capture initgen + first decode tokens for latency-sensitive traffic.
Attention-cost estimator uses a lightweight attention density probe that runs during prefill and provides a per-request cost score (0..1) used for kernel selection.
Fairness smoothing uses token-credit amortization: tenants accumulate microcredits for low-latency allocations and spend them during bursts to avoid starvation.
This approach tries to minimize changes to existing arbitration loop: we add hooks for micro-reservoir admission and a fallback path to legacy allocator on overload.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Asha: Draft design uploaded to Confluence. Initial perf hypothesis: small prompts (<=64) will benefit most from switching to low-latency kernels while preserving throughput for long sessions.

2026-03-02 - Marco: Completed baseline simulator harness. Early runs show 12% p99 improvement but throughput drop ~7% on synthetic uniform long prompts. Need tuning of reservoir size and demotion thresholds.
2026-03-04 - Design review with PM/Infra: agreed to add tenant-level credit caps and an emergency demotion to avoid noisy-tenant blowups. Action: add conservative defaults and telemetry dims.
2026-03-06 - Perf team: PR #3817 created with micro-reservoir admission and kernel-probe stubs. Linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3817
2026-03-08 - QA: added e2e workflow (small cluster) for A/B toggle. Observed an implementation bug where KV-cache warming was skipped for hedged micro-reservoirs; fixed in PR #3824.
2026-03-10 - Marco: Updated estimator to include attention sparsity signal. p99 improved to 17% on mixed traffic (50/50 short/long), throughput impact reduced to ~3%.
2026-03-12 - PM review: approved canary rollout to two internal Dedicated customers with feature flag and telemetry; product asks for additional cost accounting by token-class (init vs decode).
test_plan: Unit tests for kernel-probe and estimator logic
Simulator regression suite covering short-only, long-only, and mixed workloads
CI e2e job that runs on a small GPU pool with controlled tenant mixes and records p50/p95/p99 and throughput
Canary A/B with logging of kernel selection, attention-cost, token credits, and SLO signals
rollout_plan: Stage 2: canary on two internal Dedicated customers (2 weeks), collect telemetry
Stage 3: gradual rollout on hosted fleet (region-by-region) with automatic rollback on regression
Stage 4: enable default for new deployments after 8 weeks of stable metrics
measurement_metrics: p99 latency (initgen and first 8 decode tokens)
cost delta (estimated token compute cost) by kernel variant
